Issue: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-github/issues/228. The dispatch step polls until it can land the PR (7200 s with github.token, 2400 s with an app token, over 120/40 attempts). The caller CI it waits for needs runners from the same free-tier account pool: between 10:00Z and 12:00Z on 2026-11-09, 77 fleet runs queued while 8 ran; a scheduled sync sat in that step from 10:27Z, holding a runner while waiting for CI that could not start. An automation job must never wait in-job for work that competes for the same runner pool.

Plan: dispatch caller CI, arm GitHub native auto-merge on the owned PR, report parked runs and exit. When auto-merge cannot be armed (GITHUB_TOKEN mode, no branch protection, disabled setting), print a notice with the reason; the next scheduled sync lands the PR. Remove the whole polling class from both reusable workflows (sync and closeout), add timeout-minutes to every reusable job, add a contract test that fails on revert.
The gated sync holds a runner for up to two hours while it waits for caller CI it competes with for the same pool

value.author: pi-github228-1109
value.text: Re-review round 2 (PR 229) posted 2 additional comments outside the diff. Class rule: an armed-state flag must record an observed successful arm, never an intention. The only instance in the package is CLOSEOUT_AUTOMERGE_ALLOWED in the closeout dispatch step, which is set whenever an App deadline exists even when enable_auto_merge fell back (disabled setting, missing protection, or a failed gh pr merge). A request armed by an earlier step in the same run would then survive the always() revoke step. Fix: the flag is written only after the arm call succeeds, and the function returns a status so every fallback path is explicit. The Dependabot merge script already returns armed only after a verified request, so no second instance exists. The other outside-diff note (gh api preflight timeouts) is the reviewer's own design note marked no change required: both calls already sit inside the step's 5-minute timeout, and adding per-call timeouts would only duplicate that bound.

The shared shell captures that status before any later command, and the closeout-only block writes CLOSEOUT_AUTOMERGE_ALLOWED only when the status is true, so the always() cleanup revokes any request armed earlier in the same run instead of skipping it. patch.value:
Issue: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-github/issues/228. The dispatch step polls until it can land the PR (7200 s with github.token, 2400 s with an app token, over 120/40 attempts). The caller CI it waits for needs runners from the same free-tier account pool: between 10:00Z and 12:00Z on 2026-11-09, 77 fleet runs queued while 8 ran; a scheduled sync sat in that step from 10:27Z, holding a runner while waiting for CI that could not start. An automation job must never wait in-job for work that competes for the same runner pool.

Plan: dispatch caller CI, arm GitHub native auto-merge on the owned PR, report parked runs and exit. When auto-merge cannot be armed (no required checks, loose or unreadable freshness policy, unreadable branch rules, disabled setting), print a notice with the reason; the next scheduled sync rebuilds and retries the PR. Persistent configuration problems require maintainer attention. Remove the whole polling class from both reusable workflows (sync and closeout), add timeout-minutes to every reusable job, add a contract test that fails on revert.

No-App mode also arms the protected request: approved native PR runs can satisfy required checks, as verified on public pm-csv#241. A maintainer must approve parked native runs; the App enables unattended runs and default-branch push events. Full closeout replay is linked as separately measured publication and decision files, with the original entry point retained for existing commands.
